claims.text: The guild of butyrate-producing bacteria is polyphyletic.
Butyrate-producing bacteria cannot be accurately detected by 16S rRNA gene sequencing.
Screening 3,184 sequenced bacterial genomes identified 225 bacterial genomes with the potential to produce butyrate.
The majority of potential butyrate-producing bacterial candidates belong to distinct families within Firmicutes.
Members of nine phyla other than Firmicutes possess the potential to produce butyrate.
In stool metagenomes of healthy individuals, a mean of 19.1% of total genomes exhibit a butyrate-producing pathway.
The acetyl-CoA pathway is the most prevalent butyrate synthesis pathway in healthy human stool metagenomes, accounting for a mean of 79.7% of all pathways.
The lysine pathway represents a mean of 11.2% of all detected butyrate synthesis pathways in healthy human stool metagenomes.
The acetyl-CoA pathway in most individuals is dominated by a few firmicute groups associated with Lachnospiraceae and Ruminococcaceae.
Non-acetyl-CoA butyrate synthesis pathways in human stool metagenomes are associated primarily with Bacteroidetes.

evidence.description: and cannot be accurately detected by 16S rRNA gene sequencing.

We undertook a broad analysis of butyrate-producing pathways and individual genes by screening 3,184 sequenced bacterial genomes from the Integrated Microbial Genome database. Genomes of 225 bacteria with a potential to produce butyrate were identified, including many previously unknown candidates.
The majority of candidates belong to distinct families within the Firmicutes
members of nine other phyla, especially from Actinobacteria, Bacteroidetes, Fusobacteria, Proteobacteria, Spirochaetes, and Thermotogae, were also identified as potential butyrate producers.
A high percentage of total genomes exhibited a butyrate-producing pathway (mean, 19.1%; range, 3.2% to 39.4%)
where the acetyl-coenzyme A (CoA) pathway was the most prevalent (mean, 79.7% of all pathways)
Diversity analysis for the acetyl-CoA pathway showed that the same few firmicute groups associated with several Lachnospiraceae and Ruminococcaceae were dominating in most individuals
whereas the other pathways were associated primarily with Bacteroidetes.

methodologies.name: Genomic screening of bacterial genomes
methodologies.description: Screening 3,184 bacterial genomes from the Integrated Microbial Genome database for butyrate-producing pathways to establish a gene catalogue.

methodologies.name: Metagenomic screening of stool samples
methodologies.description: Screening stool metagenomes from healthy individuals using a gene catalogue to assess the abundance and diversity of butyrate synthesis pathways.

limitations.text: 16S rRNA gene sequencing cannot accurately detect polyphyletic butyrate-producing bacteria.
Previous investigations targeting terminal genes were incomplete due to unrecognized alternative enzymes and additional pathways.
Publicly available genomic databases are often incomplete or misannotated.

future_work.text: Understanding the specific roles of butyrate producers in health and disease.
Assisting in the development of treatments for functional dysbiosis.
